answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so influence depends on transition mass rather than claimed identities. An adversarial sybil cluster forms a sparse external cut with low conductance; min-cut and escape-probability bounds limit walks leaving it, thereby bounding its aggregate voting weight. Thus, even if a terrace of aliases mimics a zephyr or lotus, cut transitivity prevents recursive attestations from manufacturing trust.
